features.name: INT gives INTEGER
features.quote: If the declared type contains the string "INT" then it is assigned INTEGER affinity.

features.id: rule.affinity:CHAR, CLOB or TEXT gives TEXT
features.name: CHAR, CLOB or TEXT gives TEXT
features.quote: If the declared type of the column contains any of the strings "CHAR", "CLOB", or "TEXT" then that column has TEXT affinity.

features.id: rule.affinity:BLOB or no type gives BLOB
features.name: BLOB or no type gives BLOB
features.quote: If the declared type for a column contains the string "BLOB" or if no type is specified then the column has affinity BLOB.

features.id: rule.affinity:REAL, FLOA or DOUB gives REAL
features.name: REAL, FLOA or DOUB gives REAL
features.quote: If the declared type for a column contains any of the strings "REAL", "FLOA", or "DOUB" then the column has REAL affinity.

features.name: otherwise NUMERIC
features.quote: Otherwise, the affinity is NUMERIC.

features.name: the rules apply in order
features.quote: Note that the order of the rules for determining column affinity is important.

features.id: rule.expression-affinity:an IN list has no affinity
features.name: an IN list has no affinity
features.quote: The right-hand operand of an IN or NOT IN operator has no affinity if the operand is a list

features.name: a column keeps its affinity
features.quote: When an expression is a simple reference to a column of a real table (not a VIEW or subquery) then the expression has the same affinity as the table column.

features.name: an operator removes affinity
features.quote: Any operators applied to column names, including the no-op unary "+" operator, convert the column name into an expression which always has no affinity.

features.name: CAST gives its type's affinity
features.quote: has an affinity that is the same as a column with a declared type of

features.name: COLLATE keeps its operand's affinity
features.quote: A COLLATE operator has the same affinity as its left-hand side operand.

features.name: otherwise no affinity
features.quote: Otherwise, an expression has no affinity.

features.name: view and subquery columns
features.quote: the affinity for columns of a VIEW or subquery are determined by the expression affinity rules above

features.name: compound view columns
features.quote: the affinity of each column of the VIEW or subquery will be the affinity of the corresponding result column for one of the individual SELECT statements

features.id: rule.comparison:NULL is less than any value
features.name: NULL is less than any value
features.quote: A value with storage class NULL is considered less than any other value

features.name: numbers before text and blobs
features.quote: An INTEGER or REAL value is less than any TEXT or BLOB value.

features.name: numbers compare numerically
features.quote: When an INTEGER or REAL is compared to another INTEGER or REAL, a numerical comparison is performed.

features.name: text before blobs
features.quote: A TEXT value is less than a BLOB value.

features.name: text compares by collation
features.quote: When two TEXT values are compared an appropriate collating sequence is used to determine the result.

features.name: blobs compare by memcmp
features.quote: When two BLOB values are compared, the result is determined using memcmp().

features.id: rule.comparison:numeric affinity goes to the other operand
features.name: numeric affinity goes to the other operand
features.quote: If one operand has INTEGER, REAL or NUMERIC affinity and the other operand has TEXT or BLOB or no affinity then NUMERIC affinity is applied to the other operand.

features.id: rule.comparison:text affinity goes to an operand with none
features.name: text affinity goes to an operand with none
features.quote: If one operand has TEXT affinity and the other has no affinity, then TEXT affinity is applied to the other operand.

features.name: otherwise compared as is
features.quote: Otherwise, no affinity is applied and both operands are compared as is.

features.name: BETWEEN is two comparisons
features.quote: The expression "a BETWEEN b AND c" is treated as two separate binary comparisons

features.name: IN compares as equality
features.quote: Datatype conversions in comparisons of the form "x IN (SELECT y ...)" are handled as if the comparison were really "x=y".

features.id: rule.sort:ORDER BY orders by storage class
features.name: ORDER BY orders by storage class
features.quote: values with storage class NULL come first, followed by INTEGER and REAL values interspersed in numeric order, followed by TEXT values in collating sequence order, and finally BLOB values in memcmp() order.

features.name: GROUP BY keeps classes apart
features.quote: values with different storage classes are considered distinct, except for INTEGER and REAL values which are considered equal if they are numerically equal.

features.name: compound SELECTs compare as is
features.quote: No affinity is applied to comparison operands for the implicit comparisons associated with UNION, INTERSECT, or EXCEPT

features.name: columns default to BINARY
features.quote: If no collating function is explicitly defined, then the collating function defaults to BINARY.

features.id: rule.collation:an explicit COLLATE wins, left first
features.name: an explicit COLLATE wins, left first
features.quote: then the explicit collating function is used for comparison, with precedence to the collating function of the left operand.

features.id: rule.collation:then a column's collation, left first
features.name: then a column's collation, left first
features.quote: If either operand is a column, then the collating function of that column is used with precedence to the left operand.

features.name: otherwise BINARY
features.quote: Otherwise, the BINARY collating function is used for comparison.

features.name: the leftmost COLLATE anywhere wins
features.quote: the left most explicit collating function is used regardless of how deeply the COLLATE operators are nested

features.id: rule.collation:IN uses the left operand's collation
features.name: IN uses the left operand's collation
features.quote: The collating sequence used for expressions of the form "x IN (y, z, ...)" is the collating sequence of x.

features.id: rule.collation:ORDER BY uses COLLATE, then the column's
features.name: ORDER BY uses COLLATE, then the column's
features.quote: Otherwise, if the expression sorted by an ORDER BY clause is a column, then the collating sequence of the column is used to determine sort order.
